Independently downloaded with curl and opened with PyMuPDF; page count is 1.

notes: Independent review against freshly downloaded sources; research files were not edited. checked counts 117 field or assertion groups, not every repeated numerical cell: 39 core field checks (5 people values, date_utc, one_line, status_why, 13 non-null aircraft descriptions/dimensions, 11 route values or waypoint assertions, and 7 site fields), all 46 event entries including timing and all 3 verbatim quotes, all 8 numbers entries, all 20 perspective claims/evidence entries, the direct.js EgyptAir add point and source-backed buildNote content, the EgyptAir menu label/status, and the s13 page-count assertion. Primary evidence: s1 printed pp.1-9,18-19,24-25,34-39,47-67; s2 pp.2-6; s3 printed pp.74-76, with the relevant table pages visually inspected; s4 transcript printed pp.34-38 visually inspected because its text encoding is unreliable; s6 printed pp.95-114, relevant mechanical/radar discussion and pp.139-142; s7 background and test discussion; s8 chronology and controller interviews; s9 pp.1-3; s10 section 2.2.2/PDF p.29; s11 KJFK/HECA CSV records; and the s12 original photograph and dated file page. All three event quotes match the official English transcript in wording, attribution and timestamps. EST +5 hours is correct for the accident sequence after the clock change (s1 p.2 footnote 2); the ATC report already uses UTC. Eastern and western debris-field DMS coordinates convert correctly; 230 ft equals 70.104 m and is reasonably rounded to 70 m. Airport coordinates/elevations match the cited current CSV and are explicitly presented as context rather than 1999 flight fixes. No substantive factual or fairness error was established in the reviewed assertions. The NTSB conclusion is attributed and its undetermined reason and unrecorded pilot-control forces are disclosed. ECAA mechanical and traffic-avoidance positions are presented as disputed hypotheses, accompanied by the NTSB tests and radar-interference findings; no proven motive, intruding aircraft or component failure is asserted. No passenger is named and no gratuitous detail was found. The direct.js block cites only s1; its added estimated impact time is supported by s1 p.39. That block has no eventTimes, overlays or endTitle fields. The source-backed reconstruction statements in buildNote agree with s1; the renderer implementation of dead reckoning and threefold visual exaggeration cannot be independently certified from the supplied direction block. Exact final position and trajectory remain uncertain: the site coordinates identify a seabed debris-field center, and s1 p.39 warns of potentially large altitude errors during the second descent. All 16 listed source URLs returned HTTP 200 with downloaded content; all 12 PDF URLs opened as PDFs. This is not an exhaustive audit of the 140 track rows, all environment rows, every source-note assertion, or the claimed 2024-2026 search history. The only source-note error reported is directly established by the downloaded document.
